mission: Build Universal Round U.1 as the first early-universal-design layer for MathTeach, connecting motivation, belonging, psychological safety, productive error use, equity-aware design, scarcity-aware design, and UDL before disorder-specific support systems.
collection_principles: Treat equity, inclusion, and neurodiversity-aware design as early architecture constraints rather than late optional features.
Prefer official frameworks and highly cited primary or synthesis sources that can be translated into concrete tutor behavior.
Keep the tutor non-therapeutic and non-diagnostic while still using psychologically informed design constraints.
Translate all U.1 evidence into system rules for pacing, tone, feedback, representation, and friction reduction.

domains.name: Motivation Systems
domains.goal: Model autonomy, competence, relatedness, and motivational quality as part of tutoring design.

domains.name: Belonging and Psychological Safety
domains.goal: Help the tutor create conditions where learners can ask, err, and persist without shame.

domains.name: Learning from Errors
domains.goal: Treat errorful learning and corrective feedback as core parts of instruction.

domains.name: Equity and Scarcity Constraints
domains.goal: Design for low-friction learning under conditions of stress, limited resources, and stereotype threat.

domains.name: UDL and Multimodal Accessibility
domains.goal: Reduce barriers early through multiple means of representation, engagement, and expression.

starter_sources.title: Self-Determination Theory and the Facilitation of Intrinsic Motivation, Social Development, and Well-Being
starter_sources.why_it_matters: Core source for autonomy, competence, and relatedness as psychologically basic conditions for high-quality motivation.

starter_sources.title: A Question of Belonging: Race, Social Fit, and Achievement
starter_sources.organization: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
starter_sources.why_it_matters: Foundational evidence that belonging uncertainty can alter achievement and persistence, with direct implications for tutor tone and framing.

starter_sources.title: Psychological Safety and Learning Behavior in Work Teams
starter_sources.why_it_matters: Canonical source for treating safety as a condition for risk-taking, learning behavior, and error visibility.

starter_sources.title: Learning from Errors
starter_sources.why_it_matters: Strong synthesis on when and why errorful learning with corrective feedback helps retention and understanding.

starter_sources.title: Poverty Impedes Cognitive Function
starter_sources.why_it_matters: Critical evidence that scarcity can consume cognitive bandwidth, which directly matters for low-friction tutor design.

starter_sources.title: Stereotype Threat and the Intellectual Test Performance of African Americans
starter_sources.organization: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
starter_sources.why_it_matters: Foundational evidence that evaluative framing and identity threat can change performance, with direct implications for tutor wording and framing.

starter_sources.title: Inclusion and Education: All Means All
starter_sources.why_it_matters: Major inclusion framework for treating exclusion by poverty, disability, language, and background as structural educational design issues.

starter_sources.title: CAST Universal Design for Learning Guidelines 3.0
starter_sources.why_it_matters: Primary framework for reducing barriers through multiple means of engagement, representation, and action and expression.
